reviewer_statement: Developer-reviewed scientific source-semantic parity for the Python 1.2 mathematical result and return schema. Existing source comparisons plus new typed Python 1.2 whole-field/provenance tests for five contrast scales or both mixed covariance types with two inference scopes, invalid-domain tests and non-square arrays. Exact-head CI runs have not completed, and no independent external certification is claimed.
native_language_semantic_policy: Published source scientific numeric and provenance contract represented with native R scientific lists/matrices/arrays. Python frozen dataclass identity, exception classes, and arbitrary Python object introspection are not native R types.

case_evidence.description: Predeclared profile pair, one selected contrast scale, strict nominal level, typed prediction bootstrap source and source-shaped R scientific record.

Complete finite fixed profile predictions and retained participant bootstrap arrays for binomial probability, Poisson count, exposure-adjusted rate difference, log rate ratio, and count contrast; nontarget profiles and time order retained.

Exact fixed pair difference/ratio estimate and bootstrap samples, ddof=1 pointwise bootstrap SE, NumPy higher max-studentized quantile, rate-ratio log-scale exponentiated limits, source physical-bound warning.
Absent or duplicate target IDs, forbidden contrast type, missing target exposures, invalid confidence, nonfinite or insufficient bootstrap draws and nonpositive ratio denominator fail closed.
All source named fields, source time order, bootstrap array and contrast shape, extrapolation, physical bounds, scale and complete nested provenance. R list replaces frozen Python dataclass.
One a-priori profile contrast on the observed grid only, with un-clipped probability difference bounds, no familywise multiple-contrast correction and no automatic pair selection.

independent_review_status: Author-reviewed, source-pinned evidence only; exact-head CI and independent review outstanding.
language_specific_limits: R scientific records are analogous to Python typed dataclass results but cannot satisfy Python isinstance/identity semantics.
Source-produced finite observed-grid scientific arrays and errors are compared, rather than accepting arbitrary unvalidated Python objects.
Author-reported scientific parity is separate from exact-head CI, independent certification and release qualification.
